The first primitive establishes that profit emerges from risk-bearing and institutional support, forming a foundational lens for GSI’s Bayesian inference on innovation viability. The second primitive models the finite window of exclusive returns before competitor mimicry erodes value—this maps directly to GSE’s state-transition logic where innovation states evolve into competitive equilibria. The third primitive underscores the futility of static protections, implying that even legal monopolies are ephemeral. This aligns with GSI’s probabilistic modeling of legal expiry and GSE’s simulation of market saturation. These primitives form a dual structure: one of temporal constraint and one of institutional resilience, both critical for understanding how innovations become embedded in economic systems.
